clue.text: Reject crumbly bread

indicators.note: bread that is crumbly falls apart, so its letters break up and are rebuilt

explanation.surface: Someone sends back a loaf because it is falling to bits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crumbly' signals an anagram: BREAD is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To bar someone is to shut them out, a synonym for rejecting them.

clue.text: Miss in credit and so more reticent

indicators.note: the word in tells us one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: CR is the standard accounting abbreviation for credit
to miss something is to lose it, as a chance

explanation.surface: Someone missing out on credit becomes more tight-lipped as a result.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts LOSE inside CR; 'Miss' looks like a woman's title but is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who keeps things closer to the chest is more secretive, so the comparative means more reserved.

clue.text: Diana's hair gives much trouble

parts.note: Di is the short form of Diana, and the possessive adds S
a tress is a lock of hair

explanation.surface: A woman's hair is causing her a great deal of bother.
explanation.definitionFit: Distress is severe anguish or hardship, a great deal of trouble.

clue.text: Few cut a Liberal

parts.note: to sever is to cut through
L is the usual abbreviation for Liberal in politics

explanation.surface: A handful of people make cuts to a Liberal politician.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe a small number of things, more than two but not many.

clue.text: Keep a little cash to make a booking

parts.note: P, a penny, is a small coin of British money
to reserve is to book a table or seat in advance

explanation.surface: Someone holds back a few coins to secure a reservation.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep something safe from decay or harm is to conserve it, the verb's main sense.

clue.text: A top man must be firm over decoration and regal insignia

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm
MM is the Military Medal, a British award for bravery
taken as written
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the royal cipher of the Queen

explanation.surface: A senior figure in authority must stand firm on matters of medals and royal emblems.
explanation.walkthrough: MM is the Military Medal; ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen's cipher.
explanation.definitionFit: A commander is a leader in charge of others, an officer at the top.

clue.text: Made a speech — a challenge indeed!

indicators.note: the first part of indeed is read on its own, telling us to put one piece inside deed

parts.note: taken as written, the second half of the word indeed
a claim is a challenge, as when laying claim to a title

explanation.surface: Someone reacts to an orator, calling the speech quite a provocation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'indeed' is split into 'in deed': 'in' puts CLAIM inside DEED, giving DE-CLAIM-ED.
explanation.definitionFit: To declaim is to deliver a speech in a rhetorical manner, so the past tense means orated.

clue.text: Children meditate so

explanation.surface: Young people are thinking things over in this way.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a family of offspring, the other is a verb for dwelling gloomily on a matter.

clue.text: Support needed by theatrical folk

definitions.meaning: a pole or beam that holds something up
a stage ... is an object used by actors in a play

explanation.surface: Actors require some backing.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a physical brace, the other is short for property, an item used on stage.

clue.text: Recording test-case wrongly brought

indicators.note: a case brought wrongly is put together incorrectly, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A legal test case was brought improperly, and the recording proves it.
explanation.definitionFit: A cassette is a tape containing a recording of music or speech.

clue.text: About all, note, wanted to make a fresh start

parts.note: re means about or concerning
a sum is the total, the whole amount
E is a musical note

explanation.surface: On the subject of everything, someone noted a wish to begin again.
explanation.definitionFit: To begin again after a pause is the verb's main sense.

clue.text: Some consider seasoning essential for tongue

indicators.note: some of the following words is taken, so the letters lie within them

explanation.surface: Some think seasoning essential for the palate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' signals that the letters run across considER SEasoning.
explanation.definitionFit: Erse is the Gaelic language of Scotland or Ireland, and tongue means language.

clue.text: The candidate may well be partisan

indicators.note: the word partisan may well be something else, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone standing for office is likely to be biased.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may well be' signals an anagram of PARTISAN.
explanation.definitionFit: An aspirant is someone seeking a position, such as a hopeful for office.

clue.text: The person with a simple answer to all complaints

definitions.text: The person with a simple answer to all complaints

parts.words: The person with a simple answer to all complaints
parts.note: a simple is an old word for a medicinal plant, and complaints are ailments, so this is someone who treats illness with plant remedies

explanation.surface: Someone always has an easy solution to every grumble.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'simple' is an old term for a medicinal herb, and 'complaints' are illnesses rather than grumbles.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who treats ailments with plant remedies is a practitioner of herbal medicine.

clue.text: Sap exercises back in formal wear

indicators.note: the word in tells us one piece goes inside the formal wear

parts.note: dress, as in evening dress, is formal clothing

indicators.note: back means the exercises abbreviation is turned to read the other way

parts.note: PE is physical education, school exercises

explanation.surface: A fool does exercises backwards while dressed for a formal occasion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns PE into EP, and 'in' puts it inside DRESS.
explanation.definitionFit: To sap is to weaken or drain spirits, and to depress is to lower them.

clue.text: Fence in a girls compound

indicators.note: compound as a verb means to mix together, so these letters are combined anew

explanation.surface: A group of girls is kept behind a fence in an enclosure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'compound' signals an anagram of INAGIRLS; it looks like a noun for an enclosure.
explanation.definitionFit: Railings are a barrier of upright bars, a kind of fence.

clue.text: Called for as arranged

definitions.meaning: to have ... something is to have requested it

explanation.surface: Something was requested as planned.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is requested or commanded, the other is placed in proper sequence.

clue.text: A slight fall, naturally

parts.note: a fall here is precipitation from the sky, and a slight one is a single drop of the wet weather nature sends

explanation.surface: Someone took a minor tumble, as was to be expected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fall' suggests a tumble, but it means precipitation; 'naturally' points to weather.
explanation.definitionFit: A single drop of water from clouds is the smallest possible shower.

clue.text: Venture quietly to lead 11

parts.note: P, piano, is the musical direction for playing quietly
refers to the answer to 11 across, meaning start again

explanation.surface: Someone dares softly to take charge of number eleven.
explanation.walkthrough: P comes first because 'to lead' puts it in front; '11' is the answer to 11 across.
explanation.definitionFit: To venture an opinion is to dare to suppose, which is to take the liberty of assuming.

clue.text: He'd shrink from a game, right?

parts.note: bridge is a card game

explanation.surface: Someone shies away from a match, asking whether that is right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shrink' looks like shying away, but it means making a text shorter.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who shortens a book or text cuts it down, making it smaller.

clue.text: Turns and runs

definitions.meaning: a go is a turn in a game, as in whose go is it
an engine or machine ... when it operates

explanation.surface: Someone takes turns and dashes off.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is plural of a go, a turn in a game; the other is the verb for working or operating.

clue.text: The Italian no longer gets holly

parts.note: il is the Italian for the
ex means former, no longer current

explanation.surface: An Italian man is no longer in a relationship and gets some holly.
explanation.definitionFit: Ilex is the botanical genus name of the holly tree.

clue.text: Such mistakes upset a seaman in time

indicators.note: the word in tells us the sailor goes inside the period

parts.note: an era is a period of time

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so read the sailor's word backwards

parts.note: a tar is a sailor, a seaman

explanation.surface: Errors like these upset a sailor on duty in good time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns TAR into RAT, and 'in' puts it inside ERA.
explanation.definitionFit: Errata are listed printing errors in a book, the plural of erratum.

clue.text: Make up-and make-up's inapt

indicators.note: make-up is the composition of something, so the word inapt is reconstituted

explanation.surface: Someone says that making up is badly suited, and so is cosmetics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make-up's' signals an anagram of INAPT, punning on 'Make up' as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To apply cosmetics to the face is to paint it.

clue.text: Sound location for fish

indicators.note: sound tells us the word is heard rather than read, so a similar-sounding word is meant

parts.note: a place is a location

explanation.surface: A good spot to catch fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' looks like an adjective for a good location, but it signals a homophone.
explanation.definitionFit: Plaice is a flatfish eaten in Britain.

clue.text: Is, are odd-very odd in a way

indicators.note: very odd means strangely put, so these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone muses that things are strange, very strange.
explanation.walkthrough: 'very odd' signals an anagram of ISAREODD.
explanation.definitionFit: A side road is a minor road, a way off the main route.

clue.text: Employment of superior individual showing great wisdom

parts.note: U is the abbreviation for upper class, superior
a sage is a wise person

explanation.surface: A job for a top-class wise person.
explanation.walkthrough: U is upper class, a convention for superior.
explanation.definitionFit: Usage is the way something is used, its application or use.

clue.text: Signal to bring in a social worker

parts.note: to import is to bring goods in from abroad
an ant is a social insect and a worker ant

explanation.surface: A sign is made to admit someone in social services.
explanation.walkthrough: 'social worker' looks like a welfare officer, but it is an ant, a social insect; 'Signal' is an adjective meaning notable.
explanation.definitionFit: Signal as an adjective means striking or notable, as in a signal success.
